fixes.explanation: That's a fair thing to wonder, friend, but Moses doesn't ask about gods here. His words are to see “…whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.” (Numbers 13:18). He wants to know how strong they are and how many there are. It's like peeking at how long the line is before you walk in the door.

Yes, baker! Moses asks, “Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?” (Numbers 13:19). Those are the two choices he puts on the table. So the spies are scouting the cities as well as the people.

Close, but Moses really does ask this. He says, “Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?” (Numbers 13:19). So the spies have to look at the cities too, not only the people. It's an easy line to skim past, friend, so no shame.

Fruit it is, baker! Moses says, “Be courageous and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (Numbers 13:20). He asks for fruit, and he asks them to be courageous in the same breath. The text also adds that it was the season for the first ripe grapes.

That's not what the spies say, friend. They tell Moses, “…it is flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27). Right after that they say, “Here is some of its fruit!” Dry and thorny isn't anywhere in their description.
Not this time, baker. The spies say, “…it is flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27). They also say, “Here is some of its fruit!” Small and rocky isn't how they describe the land here.

That's him, baker! The text says, “Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said…” (Numbers 13:30). Caleb is the spy from the tribe of Judah (Numbers 13:6). Quieting a crowd is a real talent. I can't even quiet my oven timer.

Right, baker! Their bad report says, “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.” (Numbers 13:32). They never call the land too dry to grow anything. Earlier they said it's “…flowing with milk and honey.” (Numbers 13:27), and they showed the congregation the fruit (Numbers 13:26).

Little children is a fair guess, friend, but it's not the picture they use. They say, “We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight…” (Numbers 13:33). Even a child gets to be a person in that picture. I think the grasshopper shows how small they felt.

Sheep is a reasonable guess, baker, but that's not the picture they use. They say, “We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight…” (Numbers 13:33). A flock at least has some numbers going for it, while a grasshopper is one little jumper all by itself. I think that shows how small they felt.
